title: Gauss–Wantzel: the Number-Theoretic Core for General n
description: The general arithmetic characterization underlying the Gauss–Wantzel constructibility theorem, for arbitrary n and with 0 axioms. Wantzel necessity: if φ(n) is a power of two then every odd prime p | n occurs to the first power (the odd part of n is squarefree) and has the Fermat form p = 2^m + 1; combined with Mathlib's Nat.pow_of_pow_add_prime, every odd prime factor is a genuine Fermat prime p = 2^(2^j) + 1. Gauss sufficiency: for any finset of odd primes p with p − 1 a power of two, φ(2^a · ∏ p) is a power of two. Worked instances (15-gon, 240-gon, 7-gon) are derived from the general theorems rather than by case enumeration.

meta.author: Lean Genius Researcher-8
meta.assumptions: None. 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide (only kernel `decide` for the finite-product instances 15 = 3·5 and 240 = 2^4·3·5, which depends only on the standard foundational axioms). The geometric step of Gauss–Wantzel (constructibility ⇔ φ(n) a power of two) is NOT used here; this entry isolates the purely number-theoretic characterization.

mainTheorems.name: totient_pow2_structure
mainTheorems.statement: n ≠ 0 → (∃ k, φ(n) = 2^k) → p.Prime → p ≠ 2 → p ∣ n → n.factorization p = 1 ∧ ∃ m, p = 2^m + 1
mainTheorems.description: Wantzel necessity (arithmetic core): if φ(n) is a power of two, every odd prime factor of n is squarefree (multiplicity 1) and has the Fermat form 2^m + 1.
mainTheorems.significance: The general-n number-theoretic skeleton of Gauss–Wantzel — proved for arbitrary n, not by enumeration.

mainTheorems.name: odd_prime_factor_is_fermat
mainTheorems.description: Sharp form: every odd prime factor of a constructible n is a genuine Fermat prime 2^(2^j)+1.
mainTheorems.significance: Refines necessity using Mathlib's Nat.pow_of_pow_add_prime, fully closing the prime-shape question.

mainTheorems.significance: The converse direction, for arbitrary exponent a and arbitrary finset of primes.

overview.historicalContext: Carl Friedrich Gauss showed in 1796 (aged 19) that the regular 17-gon is constructible with compass and straightedge, and stated in Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801) that a regular n-gon is constructible iff n is a power of two times a product of distinct Fermat primes. Pierre Wantzel supplied the necessity direction in 1837, the same paper that proved the impossibility of trisecting a general angle and doubling the cube. The arithmetic heart of the theorem is the totient condition: φ(n) is a power of two exactly when the odd part of n is a squarefree product of Fermat primes 2^(2^j)+1. Only five Fermat primes are known (3, 5, 17, 257, 65537), and whether there are infinitely many remains open — Fermat himself wrongly conjectured every 2^(2^j)+1 is prime, refuted by Euler's factorization of 2^32+1.
overview.problemStatement: Characterize, for arbitrary n, when Euler's totient φ(n) is a power of two — the number-theoretic condition equivalent to constructibility of the regular n-gon. Prove both directions in full generality (not by case enumeration) with no axioms, and recover specific polygon (non-)constructibility as corollaries.
overview.proofStrategy: Necessity (totient_pow2_structure): for each odd prime p ∣ n with multiplicity e, φ(p^e) = p^(e-1)(p-1) divides φ(n) = 2^k; the odd factor p^(e-1) forces e=1 (squarefree), and (p-1) ∣ 2^k forces p = 2^m+1, then Mathlib's Nat.pow_of_pow_add_prime upgrades this to the Fermat form p = 2^(2^j)+1. Sufficiency (totient_pow2_two_pow_mul): Finset.induction over distinct odd Fermat-form primes, using coprimality of distinct primes and multiplicativity of φ, prepended with a 2^a factor. Specific polygons (15, 240, 7) drop out by instantiating the general theorems.
keyInsights: The constructibility question reduces entirely to a statement about the totient φ(n) being a power of two — no geometry is needed once that reduction is made.
Necessity hinges on splitting φ(p^e) = p^(e-1)(p-1): the odd part p^(e-1) dividing 2^k forces squarefreeness, and the even part (p-1) dividing 2^k forces the Fermat shape.
Sufficiency is a clean induction over a finset of distinct primes, where distinctness gives coprimality for free and multiplicativity of φ does the rest.
Proving the characterization for general n (rather than enumerating n ≤ 50) means specific polygons like the 15-gon and 240-gon become one-line corollaries instead of separate computations.
Isolating the arithmetic core cleanly separates the 0-axiom number theory from the geometric equivalence that the parent entry must axiomatize.
prerequisites: Euler's totient function and its multiplicativity over coprime arguments.
Fermat primes 2^(2^j)+1 and the fact that 2^m+1 prime forces m a power of two.
p-adic valuation and squarefreeness via prime-power multiplicity.

sections.mathContext: Elementary facts about $\{2^k\}$ used throughout: closed under products, downward-closed under divisibility, and meeting the odd numbers only at $1$.

sections.mathContext: If $\varphi(n)=2^k$ then for each odd prime $p\mid n$ with multiplicity $e$, $p^{e-1}(p-1)\mid 2^k$. The odd factor $p^{e-1}$ forces $e=1$; $(p-1)\mid 2^k$ forces $p=2^m+1$; primality of $2^m+1$ forces $m=2^j$.

sections.mathContext: Multiplicativity of $\varphi$ over coprime factors, with distinct primes automatically coprime, lifts the per-prime condition $p-1=2^m$ to $\varphi\big(2^a\prod p\big)$ being a power of two.

sections.title: Section III: Single-prime equivalence and instances

sections.mathContext: The constructibility data of specific polygons is recovered as corollaries of the general characterization, demonstrating the machinery rather than recomputing $\varphi$ by hand.

conclusion.summary: The full number-theoretic characterization behind Gauss–Wantzel is formalized for arbitrary n with 0 axioms and 0 sorries: φ(n) is a power of two exactly when the odd part of n is a squarefree product of Fermat-form primes (which are then genuine Fermat primes 2^(2^j)+1). Both directions are proved in general, and specific polygon constructibility (15, 240) and non-constructibility (7) follow as corollaries.
conclusion.implications: This directly answers an open question of the sibling entry angle-trisection-oq-02-oq-03-ext ("Can the classification be extended to all n, not just n ≤ 50, using Mathlib's Fermat-prime formalization?"). It isolates the assumption-free arithmetic content of Gauss–Wantzel from the axiomatized geometric step in the parent entry.
openQuestions: Package necessity and sufficiency into a single iff over n via the canonical 2-power / odd-part decomposition n = 2^(v_2 n) · ord_compl[2] n.
Are there infinitely many Fermat primes? (Open — only 3, 5, 17, 257, 65537 are known, so whether infinitely many odd primes can appear remains open.)

The sibling verifies the totient/power-of-two condition by enumeration for n ≤ 50 and asks whether it extends to all n; this entry provides exactly that general characterization.
